page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-48 is a compute-focused virtual machine powered by a 2.3 GHz Intel Xeon 8581C processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 48 vCPUs across 24 dedicated physical cores with multithreading enabled. It features 96 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Processor hardware includes 260 MB of Level 3 cache along with hardware acceleration features such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX-Tile and AMX-INT8) and AVX-512 vector extensions. The instance is provisioned without bundled local storage and without discrete GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations position the instance in the upper quartile across multiple compute and instruction-set workloads. It scores 54,727.59 on the PassMark CPU test and achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 17,695.0. Compute-specific routines demonstrate strong execution, including Clang software compilation at 39,655.0 and ray tracing at 51,080.0, while Geekbench image processing reaches 18,505.0 to place in the top decile. In language model processing, onboard matrix acceleration drives 352.2 tokens per second in small 135M model text generation and 28.83 tokens per second on 7B parameter models. Memory throughput measures 150.28 GB/s for large uncached reads and 64.01 GB/s for writes.

The hardware configuration emphasizes compute density over memory capacity. By avoiding large memory allocations and integrated local disks, the instance provides cost efficiency for processor-saturated tasks that do not need large per-thread memory pools or low-latency local NVMe drives. Storage and network connectivity rely entirely on attached network resources. The c4-highcpu-48 is well matched for software compilation pipelines, batch compute jobs, static web serving, video and image processing, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-48 is a compute-oriented instance equipped with 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores on a 2.3 GHz Intel Xeon 8581C processor. The system provides 96 GB of RAM, yielding a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside 260 MB of L3 cache and hardware acceleration via Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions. It includes no bundled local disks or discrete GPUs. Benchmarks place the system in the top quartile for PassMark CPU performance, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Clang compilation, with image processing scoring in the top ten percent. High CPU density relative to system memory makes it a cost-effective platform for workloads that do not require high memory-to-core ratios. The instance is recommended for CI/CD compilation runners, batch compute processing, static web serving, and CPU-driven machine learning inference tasks.
